harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Inventory application is available on node1 at TCP port 8181 under an enforcing AppArmor profile. It persists across reboot while retaining Ubuntu 7.10 and kernel 2.6.22-14-generic.
actions_performed: Created a Python 2.5-compatible inventory HTTP application and data endpoint.
Configured a SysV service running as www-data with automatic boot startup.
Created and loaded an AppArmor 2.1 profile in enforce mode.
Verified root, health, and inventory API responses through node1's managed IP.
Rebooted node1 safely and verified boot identity changed, service recovery, data integrity, and continued AppArmor enforcement.

evidence.requirement: Serve the inventory application over TCP port 8181
evidence.summary: Listener and HTTP 200 responses confirm the inventory root, health endpoint, and inventory API are available on port 8181, including after reboot.
AppArmor reports the inventory profile in enforce mode, and the live service process label is /usr/local/sbin/inventory-server (enforce), before and after reboot.

evidence.requirement: Retain the installed legacy OS release and kernel
evidence.summary: Node remains Ubuntu 7.10 with kernel 2.6.22-14-generic; the implementation uses installed Python 2.5 and SysV init.

evidence.requirement: node1 mandatory restart and recovery protocol
evidence.summary: Healthy baseline boot ID b2bcf8e6-1b11-4d04-a9b8-f08123e714fa was captured, reboot acknowledged, new boot ID f7313da0-0b67-4b6e-af25-f2c313a52d87 observed, and service, listener, AppArmor confinement, HTTP health, API data, and matching data checksum recovered.
